newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN IN SHOCK FIRST GAME DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN IN SHOCK FIRST GAME DEFEAT.

text.p: German league champions Bayern Munich suffered a shock defeat in their first game of the season to newly-promoted Kaiserslautern in front of a sell-out Munich home crowd on Saturday.
An 80th-minute goal by the Dane Michael Schjonberg was enough to secure a 1-0 victory for Kaiserslautern, back in the top league after a one-year absence.
Bayern never showed their winning form of last year and were without key players including Ghanian international Sammy Kuffour and striker Alexander Zickler for the clash.

"We simply didn't do enough to win. But we shouldn't think the worst and now must do some careful analysis," said Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni after the game, which was watched by some 63,000 spectators.
Kaiserlautern coach Otto Rehhagel said the victory, their first on Bayern territory for 14 years, was an early boost for their season.
"Just after being promoted, a win like this is particularly good. It will give a real boost to our self-confidence," he told reporters.
Wolfsburg, who secured promotion along with Kaiserslautern last season, also won their first game, beating last year's relegation battlers Rostock 1-0 with a last minute goal by Roy Praeger.

Cologne, hoping to improve on last season's mediocre performance after a string of new signings, came from behind twice to beat Duisberg 3-2 with a 76th-minute close-range shot from Austrian striker Toni Polster.
With UEFA Cup winners Schalke having made a winning start on Friday with a 2-1 victory over Bayer Leverkusen, all eyes are now on European Cup-winners Borussia Dortmund's first outing on Sunday.

Dortmund, seen as one of three leading championship contenders this season, travel to Berlin to play Hertha Berlin, back in the first division with a new foreign signing in Dutch international Brian Roy.
